capability_bindings.label: Fleet Operations
capability_bindings.structure: conceptual presentation, not canonical capability topology

model_fields.purpose: Keep aircraft ready. Deliver the schedule.
model_fields.intro: Fleet Operations connects aircraft readiness, crew coordination and day-of-flight recovery.
model_fields.economics: Aircraft earn through flying, while maintenance, fuel and disruption consume resources. Availability and schedule reliability influence how productive the fleet can be.
model_fields.people: Illustrative roles: flight operations, engineering and crew planning. Coordination links aircraft readiness with the flying schedule.
model_fields.data: Illustrative inputs: aircraft condition, maintenance requirements, crew availability and disruption status.
model_fields.dependencies: Aircraft, airports, air navigation and maintenance are enabling dependencies.
forces: Aircraft availability meets the flying schedule
Maintenance constraints and disruption can reduce productive flying time. This is an operating mechanism, not a measured easyJet loss or unmet buying need.
model_fields.changing_scope: Connectivity is passenger-service context; Jetstream is a historical operations announcement. Neither demonstrates current fleet performance.

capability_bindings.label: Network Planning
capability_bindings.structure: conceptual presentation, not canonical capability topology

model_fields.purpose: Put capacity where it can create value.
model_fields.intro: Network Planning connects destinations, schedule choices and available aircraft capacity.
model_fields.economics: Route choice and flight timing shape the seats available to sell. Demand, fares, seasonality and operating cost influence route contribution; route counts alone do not measure profitability.
model_fields.people: Illustrative roles: network planners, commercial teams and operations. Planning reconciles demand expectations with aircraft and airport constraints.
model_fields.data: Illustrative inputs: booking patterns, seasonal demand, schedules and capacity.
model_fields.dependencies: Aircraft capacity and airport access constrain feasible schedules.
forces: Seasonality changes the value of capacity
A route can serve different demand and cost conditions across the year. The retained network count establishes scale, not route-level market share, yield or an available sales opportunity.
model_fields.changing_scope: Booking discovery is adjacent commercial-channel context; the announcement does not establish a change in this capability.

capability_bindings.label: Customer Service
capability_bindings.structure: conceptual presentation, not canonical capability topology

model_fields.intro: Customer Service connects booking support with assistance when a journey changes.
model_fields.economics: Resolution effort, refunds and customer experience interact during disruption. Self-service can change the service mix; this prototype does not quantify savings or retention.
model_fields.people: Illustrative roles: customer service teams, digital service and airport operations. Handoffs matter when a flight or booking changes.
model_fields.data: Illustrative inputs: booking details, flight status and customer contact.
model_fields.dependencies: Digital channels and airport operations support the service journey.
forces: Service obligations depend on the flight and circumstances. A sector obligation does not establish a company failing or a new procurement.
model_fields.changing_scope: Booking discovery is adjacent commercial-channel context; the announcement does not establish a change in this capability.
